court_fees.publisher: New York State, Civil Practice Law and Rules

mandatory.label: Index number
mandatory.note: $190 for the index number, plus $5 to the records management fund and $15 to the cultural education account. Buying the index number is what starts the case.

mandatory.label: Request for Judicial Intervention
mandatory.note: The filing that puts the case in front of a judge.

mandatory.label: Note of issue
mandatory.note: The additional amount for placing the cause on the calendar. The statute sets $125 for the two together.

conditional.label: Each motion or cross motion
conditional.note: Charged every time either side asks the judge to decide something.

conditional.label: Demand for a jury trial
conditional.note: Only the grounds for the divorce can go to a jury, and since New York added a no-fault ground in 2010 almost nothing does.

conditional.label: Filing a stipulation of settlement
conditional.note: The fee for agreeing, which is the cheapest line on the list.

conditional.label: Certified copy of the judgment
conditional.note: $8 in New York City, the Bronx, Kings, Queens, Richmond, Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester and Rockland; $4 in every other county. Most people need at least one, to change a name or a title or a beneficiary.

conditional.label: Certificate of exemplification
conditional.note: $25 in the same counties, $10 elsewhere. Needed to use the judgment out of state.

waiver.title: Motion to waive costs, fees, and expenses
waiver.note: A party who swears out an affidavit of their income and assets showing they lack sufficient means may be relieved of the costs, fees and expenses entirely. A party represented by a legal aid society or a nonprofit legal services organisation gets the waiver without having to move for it.

court_fees.note: Set by statute, so these are the only figures on the subject that are not an estimate. A county clerk may charge for copies and searches on top.

survey.what: divorce study of readers who had recently been through a divorce
limits: Respondents volunteered: they had given an email address while researching how to hire a divorce lawyer, so the sample is people who were shopping for one.
It is national. Nothing in it is specific to New York.
It reports what people remembered paying, not what any firm billed.

outcomes.label: Uncontested, with a lawyer
outcomes.note: Nothing in dispute by the time the lawyer was hired

outcomes.label: Disputed, then settled
outcomes.note: Issues in dispute at the start, all of them agreed before trial

outcomes.label: Trial on one issue
outcomes.note: One issue the parties could not agree, decided by a judge

outcomes.label: Trial on two or more issues
outcomes.note: More than one issue decided by a judge

rates_from: src/data/research/lawyer-hourly-rates.json, so the rate used to turn hours into money is the same one the hourly rate article publishes
